stories.title: Trump says he will ban US firms from building AI data centres overseas
stories.summary: Donald Trump announced that he intends to prohibit U.S. companies from constructing AI data centres outside the United States and warned of a “tremendous tax” for firms that do so. He made the remarks at a press briefing after returning from Asia, providing little detail on how the policy would be enforced. The issue was prominent in the recent midterm elections, and firms such as Meta and Google already have overseas data‑centre agreements.
stories.why: The move could compel major tech firms to keep AI infrastructure domestic, reshaping investment and supply‑chain decisions.

stories.title: Alberta to require upfront cleanup payments for new oil and gas wells
stories.summary: Legislation in Alberta’s Energy, Environment and Utilities Statutes Amendment Act, 2026 will require oil and gas companies to make an initial payment of up to $50,000 for each well drilled after April 1, 2027, followed by yearly incremental payments over ten years. The money stays attached to the well regardless of ownership changes. Rancher Bill Heidecker, president of the Alberta Surface Rights Federation, said the measure looks good on paper but raised questions about implementation and enforcement, noting a backlog of thousands of wells still awaiting proper closure.
stories.why: It creates a dedicated fund to help address the orphan‑well problem and lower the risk of environmental harm.

stories.summary: Even older chips retain value — according to Compute Credit Index Research , some H100s are selling for about half of their original cost basis from 2023, while some H200 configurations are selling for the same price they did when introduced in 2024. stories.title: Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine's allies hold military exercise, says Tusk
stories.summary: Poland says a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace early on Friday, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying it did not appear to be an accident when Western military exercises were taking place in the region. Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said the Kh-101 missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

stories.title: European leaders say they are ready to negotiate with Russia on ending Ukraine war
stories.summary: European leaders said they are prepared to negotiate with Russia to end the war in Ukraine, stressing a united negotiating stance. UK politician Andy Burnham and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz described Moscow’s maximalist demands as unrealistic. US envoy Jared Kushner said President Trump wants a deal with Moscow “with Europe by his side,” while President Putin has rejected any European role in the US‑led peace talks.
stories.why: It indicates a possible shift toward a broader diplomatic effort to resolve the conflict.
stories.previousTitle: Europe says it is ready to negotiate with Russia to end Ukraine war
stories.previousSummary: At a Berlin summit of the “Coalition of the Willing,” European leaders said they have a united negotiating position and are prepared to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Europe is clear and consistent, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called Moscow’s maximalist demands unrealistic. US envoy Jared Kushner said President Trump wants a deal with Moscow alongside Europe, and President Vladimir Putin has rejected any European role in the US‑led peace talks.

stories.title: RBI expected to raise repo rate to 5.75% in December, 6% by February
stories.summary: A Reuters poll reported by the Economic Times indicates the Reserve Bank of India plans to increase its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December and again to 6% in February. The moves are driven by inflation moving above the RBI’s 6% tolerance limit, amid rising energy costs and uneven monsoon rainfall. The RBI is projected to deliver two more hikes by February.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: Anthropic shares fall up to 7.4% in pre‑market trade on second day
stories.summary: Anthropic’s stock dropped as much as 7.4% in pre‑market trading on its second day of listing, after a 39% surge from the IPO price on Thursday that left the shares 17% above the offering level at the close. The decline unfolded amid a global market sell‑off and concerns about the company’s steep valuation and competitive pressures in the AI sector.
stories.why: The slide reflects investor caution toward high‑valuation AI IPOs during a broader market downturn.

stories.title: Rupee appreciation may cut Indian IT firms' FY27 earnings
stories.summary: A new report says that a stronger Indian rupee could reduce earnings for Indian IT companies in fiscal year 2027. The impact is expected to be greatest for firms with sizable European client exposure, as a stronger rupee erodes foreign‑currency revenue. With traditional cost‑saving measures becoming scarce, maintaining profit margins will be harder amid a challenging pricing environment.
